HUMAN RESOURCES POLICY 1.1 Purpose and scope The Human Resources policy establishes standard people practices for Northstar Services Pvt. Ltd. (the Company). It applies to full-time employees in India unless an employment agreement, applicable law or formally approved exception states otherwise. Contractors, consultants and temporary workers are covered only where their contracts expressly include the relevant provision. 1.2 Working hours and attendance The standard work week is Monday to Friday. Normal working hours are 9:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., including a one-hour meal break. A team manager may approve a different schedule to support customer operations, project delivery or regional collaboration. Employees must record attendance using the Company's approved attendance system. Repeated attendance exceptions should be discussed with the manager and HR. Employees working remotely must remain reachable during agreed core

ystem. Repeated attendance exceptions should be discussed with the manager and HR. Employees working remotely must remain reachable during agreed core collaboration hours, protect Company information and follow the same attendance and leave-notification requirements as office-based employees. Remote work does not change the employee's obligation to meet role expectations. 1.3 Annual leave Eligible full-time employees receive 18 working days of annual leave for each completed leave year. Leave is credited at 1.5 days per completed month. New employees receive a pro-rated credit based on their joining date. Annual leave should normally be requested at least five working days in advance through the HR portal. Approval depends on team coverage, project commitments and the employee's available balance. Employees should hand over active work before starting planned leave. Unused leave carry-forward and encashment, where applicable, are governed by the Company's annual leave rules and applicable law. 1.4 Sick leave and absence notification An employee unable to work due to illness should notify the reporting manager as early as reasonably possible on the first day of absence and record the leave in the HR portal. For an absence of more than three consecutive working days, HR may request reasonable supporting documentation, subject to applicable law and privacy

For an absence of more than three consecutive working days, HR may request reasonable supporting documentation, subject to applicable law and privacy requirements. Medical information must be handled confidentially and shared only with authorised personnel. 1.5 Learning and development Employees may request role-related training through their manager. The manager should evaluate business relevance, budget availability, expected skill improvement and workload impact. Training paid by the Company may require a completion certificate or a short knowledge-sharing session. Any service commitment associated with sponsored training must be communicated in writing before enrolment.

PROCUREMENT POLICY 2.1 Purpose and procurement principles The Procurement policy defines how the Company requests, evaluates, approves and purchases goods and services. All purchases must demonstrate business need, budget availability, fair supplier consideration, appropriate approval and documented evidence. Employees must not split a purchase into smaller requests to avoid an approval threshold. 2.2 Purchase request and approval thresholds A business requester must raise a purchase requisition before committing the Company to a supplier. The requisition must describe the goods or services, quantity, business justification, expected delivery date, cost centre and proposed supplier where known. Procurement checks completeness and sourcing requirements before a purchase order is issued. The approved purchase value includes applicable taxes, freight, implementation fees and other committed charges when known at the time of approval. 2.3 Vendor onboarding A new vendor must complete the vendor onboarding process before the first purchase order is released. The vendor record should include legal name, registered address, tax registration details where applicable, bank account evidence, primary contact, service category and signed contractual

Procurement validates the submitted information, while Finance independently verifies bank details using an approved verification method. Vendor master changes, especially bank-account changes, require independent review. A requester must not approve their own vendor creation or bank-detail modification. Suspicious requests to change payment instructions must be escalated to the Finance controller and Information Security team. 2.4 Supplier evaluation Supplier evaluation should consider total cost of ownership, quality, delivery capability, information security, regulatory compliance, financial stability, support model and relevant references. The evaluation record should explain the selection decision and material trade-offs. A lower quoted price does not automatically represent the best-value supplier. 2.5 Purchase orders

ain the selection decision and material trade-offs. A lower quoted price does not automatically represent the best-value supplier. 2.5 Purchase orders and emergency procurement Only authorised Procurement personnel may issue purchase orders. Suppliers should not begin work or ship goods before receiving an approved purchase order, except under a documented emergency exception. Emergency procurement may be used only when an immediate purchase is necessary to protect people, critical operations, assets or legal compliance and the normal process cannot be completed in time. The business owner must document the reason, supplier selection, estimated value and approvals. Procurement must review the transaction retrospectively within five working days.

FINANCE AND ACCOUNTS PAYABLE POLICY 3.1 Purpose and scope This policy describes minimum controls for supplier invoices, payment processing, expense classification and financial approvals. It applies to employees who request purchases, confirm receipt, process invoices, approve expenses or release payments. 3.2 Invoice submission requirements Suppliers should submit invoices to the designated Accounts Payable mailbox or supplier portal. Each invoice must contain the supplier's legal name, invoice number, invoice date, tax details where applicable, purchase order number, description of goods or services, amount, currency and payment instructions. Incomplete invoices may be placed on hold until missing information is provided. 3.3 Three-way matching For purchase-order-backed transactions, Accounts Payable performs a three-way match between the purchase order, goods receipt or service confirmation, and supplier invoice.

The payment due date must be calculated using the contractual term and the Company's business calendar. A disputed invoice is not ready for payment until the dispute is resolved. 3.5 Invoice exceptions and holds Common reasons for an invoice hold include a missing purchase order, missing receipt confirmation, duplicate invoice number, price variance, quantity variance, invalid tax information, vendor-master mismatch or suspected fraud. Accounts Payable records the hold reason, assigns an owner and tracks the resolution date. The requester and Procurement should respond to clarification requests promptly. A suspected duplicate or fraudulent invoice must not be paid while the investigation is open. Employees must not change supplier bank details based solely on an email request. The employee's manager reviews business purpose and policy compliance. Finance checks documentation, tax treatment and expense coding. Employees cannot approve their own expenses.

INFORMATION HANDLING AND CONTROL REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Handling policy documents Employees must use approved Company repositories to store current policies, procedures, contracts and supporting records. Superseded policy versions should be marked as archived and retained according to the Company's records-retention schedule. A downloaded copy may become outdated; employees should confirm the effective version before relying on it. 4.2 Access and confidentiality Access to HR, procurement and finance records must be granted according to job responsibilities and the principle of least privilege. Employee personal data, supplier bank details, commercial pricing and payment information must not be exposed to unauthorised users. Access reviews should be performed periodically by the relevant data owner. 4.3 Records and audit trail Approvals, purchase requisitions, purchase orders, vendor changes, invoice holds, payment releases

he relevant data owner. 4.3 Records and audit trail Approvals, purchase requisitions, purchase orders, vendor changes, invoice holds, payment releases and expense claims must retain a traceable audit record. The record should identify the requester, approver, date, decision and supporting evidence. Users must not overwrite or delete approval history to conceal a change. 4.4 Exceptions A policy exception must identify the requirement being waived, business justification, risk, duration, compensating control and approving authority. Exceptions must be time-bound and reviewed before expiry. An exception does not override applicable law or contractual obligations. 5.
